distribution.title: Poisson distribution
distribution.intro: The Poisson distribution models a nonnegative count with parameter \(\lambda>0\), often the count of events in a fixed interval under a constant-rate independent-increments model.
distribution.properties: Both the mean and variance are \(\lambda\). The sum of independent Poisson variables is Poisson with parameter equal to the sum of their parameters.
distribution.course: The course uses the sum of Poisson observations as a sufficient statistic and gives a Poisson estimating-function example.
distribution.course_link: Explore sufficiency in the Poisson model
distribution.r_intro: These examples use functions from R’s stats package. For functions with d, p, q, and r prefixes, they compute a density or mass, cumulative probability, quantile, and random samples, respectively.
distribution.r_code:
dpois(2, lambda = 3)
ppois(2, lambda = 3)
qpois(0.5, lambda = 3)
rpois(100, lambda = 3)
